objects.why: the ambition of 0 to 1: a bold leap nobody has made yet
money moved between people; PayPal and the margins that competition destroys
customer lifetime value against acquisition cost, the distribution math
competition as a trap that binds the rivals
a monopoly that starts from a small, exact niche
durability: a moat that keeps competitors out
the hidden secret of ride-sharing: cars already on the road and unused demand

spine.claim: Competition is for losers: rivals who fight over the same turf become the same company, and the real goal is a monopoly built on a secret.
Progress is vertical, 0 to 1, not horizontal, 1 to n: starting small, owning distribution and the seven questions decide who builds the future.
The honest pushback: monopoly advice can be self-serving and easy to claim only after the win, and iteration still matters.
Definite optimism beats indefinite optimism: a founder who designs the future on purpose outlasts one who keeps options open.
The next great company is one nobody has named yet, built on a secret few people believe is true.
